prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions were consistently too optimistic across all tests compared to noise-corrected results.
Evidence for specific kinds of change is still thin because each category currently has only one test.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: +5.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, layout: +1.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: -5.6% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, wait_info: -0.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, hint: +1.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 66.2%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 19.4%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [finish, new_screen] Interactive Desktop Controls Sandbox: Insert a interactive sandbox screen (new_controls_sandbox) before final home intro to demonstrate pet interaction controls and hotkeys. (why: Support emails show users struggle after onboarding with how to control, hide, or talk to their pet on the desktop.)
1: [sign_in, reorder] Post-Adoption Sign-In Shift: Move sign-in after pet adoption selection so users pick their pet before creating an account. (why: Sign-in step drops 27.1% of users early; postponing authentication until after emotional investment in pet selection increases completion.)
2: [home, wait_info] Live Pet Fact Feed During Generation: Display an estimated wait timer and rotating fun pet trivia feed during the pet generation waiting screen. (why: The waiting stage has a median wait of 201s (mean 2336s), leading to user drop-off due to perceived unresponsiveness.)
3: [sign_in, copy] Account Cloud Sync Security Copy: Update sign-in screen text to emphasize that signing in protects pets from being lost or reset during app updates. (why: 8 support emails cited pets missing or resetting after signing back in.)
4: [adoption, hint] Photo Quality Assistant Hint: Add photo lighting and formatting guidance tips directly on the upload photo screen. (why: Users reported custom pet visual glitches due to improper photo uploads.)
5: [finish, layout] Spotlight Desktop Launch Focus: Reframe the home_intro screen using a spotlight layout with a bold call to action to launch the desktop companion. (why: Finish step drop-off is high (64.8% step completion) with a median time of 395s.)
6: [home, notification] Background Notification Ready Switch: Add an option on the waiting screen to notify users on their desktop background when pet setup finishes. (why: Long wait times cause users to switch away to other apps and forget onboarding.)

scores.note: Adding a new screen at finish step previously resulted in -5.6% conversion.
High drop-off step (27.1%); shifting authentication reduces friction early.
Wait info changes previously showed negative lift (-0.9%) despite high wait times.
Low cost copy tweak supported by sign-in hint benchmark (+1.5%) and support emails.
Targeting high-drop adoption step with contextual photo guidance.
Layout reframing on high drop-off finish step without adding extra screens.
Addresses high median wait time (201s) but requires background notification implementation.
